pages.title: The Crate
pages.content:
The Crate

The Crate

Every standard crate brings nine varieties of freshly harvested produce directly from our partner fields to your kitchen. Sourced from six regional farms within sixty kilometres of our packing barn, each delivery arrives on the day it is picked.

Nine Kinds from Field to Table

A standard crate holds approximately 4.5 kilograms of fresh vegetables and greens, carefully balanced across nine distinct varieties. Rather than overfilling your kitchen with surplus produce that risks wilting in the crisper drawer, we assemble a focused selection designed for a full week of home cooking. Each box typically includes crisp salad leaves or cooking greens, sturdy root crops like carrots and beets, dependable kitchen staples such as potatoes and onions, and a seasonal culinary herb. Because our six partner farms harvest everything on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, every leaf retains its natural moisture, firm texture, and field-fresh vitality when it reaches your counter.

A Four-Season Harvest Calendar

Our harvest changes continuously across the four seasons to reflect what thrives naturally in Wren Valley. In spring, crates feature crisp radishes, tender spring onions, young lettuces, and sweet early greens. Summer brings abundant leafy greens, flowering dill, sweet carrots, and fragrant herbs picked under the morning sun. As autumn arrives, our boxes transition to hearty kales, rainbow chard, earthen beets, and newly dug field potatoes. During the colder winter months, members receive robust brassicas, cold-hardy winter greens, and cured root vegetables that store exceptionally well in a domestic kitchen pantry. Every seasonal transition is handled smoothly without relying on long-distance haulage.

Kitchen Storage and Vegetable Care

Because our vegetables are harvested only hours before delivery, they arrive with significantly more vitality and a longer shelf life than typical market produce. To keep tender greens and chard crisp throughout the week, rinse them gently in cold water, shake off excess moisture, and store them wrapped in a clean linen towel inside your refrigerator. Root vegetables like carrots, beets, and potatoes prefer a cool, dark, and dry cupboard away from direct sunlight, where they remain firm for weeks. Fresh herb bundles thrive when trimmed at the stem base and placed upright in a small glass of fresh water on your kitchen worktop.

pages.title: Packing Morning
pages.content:
Packing Morning

Packing Morning

Every Tuesday and Thursday morning, our packing barn operates through a tightly timed four-hour window from dawn until dispatch. We move fresh produce from field collection to ready delivery crates in four hours flat.

5:00 — Dawn Field Harvest

The work begins at 5:00 sharp across our partner fields while the morning air is still cold and damp. Growers like Hana Moreau cut crisp lettuces and chard, while Rafael Ortiz pulls carrots and beets from moist soil before the sun warms the earth. Harvesting at first light ensures that delicate leaves remain fully hydrated and tender, locking in flavour and essential moisture. By working early, our growers avoid the heat of the day, preserving the cell structure of the vegetables and ensuring they travel from open soil to collection bins without losing their crisp texture.

7:30 — Washing and Sorting at 14 Orchard Lane

By 7:30, crates of harvested produce arrive at our central packing barn located at 14 Orchard Lane in Wren Valley. Co-founder Tomas Achebe leads the barn team through careful inspection, trimming, and cold-water rinsing in stainless steel washing troughs. Vegetables are handled gently by hand to prevent bruising. We wrap delicate bundles in unbleached breathable paper, keeping herbs and loose roots protected during transit. Every item is weighed and apportioned so that standard crates reach their 4.5-kilogram balance with nine distinct varieties cleanly arranged and ready for immediate kitchen use.

9:00 — Crate Assembly and Dispatch

By 9:00, all crates are fully assembled, covered, and stacked systematically by delivery route near the barn loading doors. Delivery lead Lena Sorensen coordinates route schedules for afternoon transport across our twelve city neighbourhoods. Because packing concludes by mid-morning, the barn returns to stillness while vehicles depart for scheduled afternoon drop-offs between 14:00 and 19:00. This disciplined four-hour routine eliminates warehousing and overnight cooling, delivering vegetables to city counters mere hours after leaving the soil.

Returned Wooden Crates and Minimal Packaging

We package all produce in sturdy, reusable wooden crates that circulate continuously between our barn and member homes. We charge a $0 crate deposit, asking only that you leave your empty wooden crate and folded paper wraps outside your doorway on your next delivery day. Lena Sorensen and our drivers collect the used crate when dropping off your fresh box, returning it to 14 Orchard Lane to be sanitized and packed again. This circular system completely eliminates single-use plastic bags and disposable shipping cartons.

pages.title: Our Growers
pages.content:
Our Growers

Our Growers

Hatake Greens partners with six independent local farms situated within sixty kilometres of our Wren Valley packing barn. By collaborating directly with dedicated regional growers, we support thoughtful land stewardship and ensure exceptional harvest quality.

A Six-Farm Regional Partnership

Our vegetable membership relies on close, long-term partnerships with six independent farms located within a sixty-kilometre radius of 14 Orchard Lane. Ines Calder, co-founder and grower relations lead, works hand in hand with farm operators throughout the planting and harvest seasons. By coordinating crop schedules well before seed goes into the ground, we establish fair prices for growers while eliminating the surplus waste common to speculative farming. This direct relationship keeps family-run acreage productive, protects local soils, and ensures our crates represent the very best produce our surrounding valley can grow.

Hana Moreau at Moreau Field

Hana Moreau manages Moreau Field, dedicating her fertile valley acreage to delicate salad leaves, tender kales, and vibrant Swiss chard. Every Tuesday and Thursday at 5:00, Hana and her field crew walk the morning rows with harvest knives, cutting greens while morning dew covers the foliage. Her careful soil management and natural cultivation practices produce leaves with exceptional sweetness, thickness, and longevity. Hana’s freshly cut greens form the crisp foundation of our weekly boxes, traveling straight from Moreau Field to our washing troughs in Wren Valley.

Rafael Ortiz at Ortiz Roots

Specializing in cool-weather root vegetables, Rafael Ortiz oversees Ortiz Roots on deep, sandy loam soils ideal for straight, sweet taproots. Rafael supplies our crates with crisp Dutch-style carrots, bright red radishes, and rich earthen beets. Rather than storing roots in climate-controlled warehouses for months, Rafael loosens and pulls them fresh on packing mornings. His commitment to traditional soil conditioning yields carrots with vibrant green tops and rich natural sugars, bringing earthy sweetness and satisfying crunch to our members' seasonal soups, roasts, and salads.

Priya Nair and Kwame Mensah

Fragrant culinary herbs are cultivated by Priya Nair at Nair Herb Garden, where parsley, dill, cilantro, and seasonal aromatics are hand-tied into fresh bundles on harvest mornings. Meanwhile, Kwame Mensah manages Mensah Hill, cultivating rolling hillside plots dedicated to newly dug field potatoes, firm yellow onions, and hearty seasonal brassicas. Working together alongside our other partner farms, Priya and Kwame ensure that every Hatake Greens box arrives balanced with bright culinary flavour notes and hearty kitchen essentials.

pages.title: Plans & Prices
pages.content:
Plans & Prices

Plans & Prices

We provide simple, transparent vegetable memberships designed to supply real home kitchens without complicated contracts. Choose the crate size and schedule that best fits your household cooking routine.

Weekly Crate Options and Pricing

We offer three crate sizes to match different household sizes, alongside an alternate-week delivery schedule. The Small crate is designed for 1–2 people, contains 6 kinds of vegetables, and costs $24 / week. Our most popular option, the Standard crate, suits 2–4 people with 9 kinds of produce weighing about 4.5 kilograms for $32 / week. For larger households of 4–6 people, the Large crate provides 12 kinds of seasonal vegetables for $44 / week. If you cook less frequently, our Every-other-week standard crate delivers 9 kinds for $34 / delivery.

Fresh Farm Add-ons

Members can easily supplement their regular vegetable box with weekly farm staples. We offer a dozen free-range eggs for $7, collected fresh from pasture-roaming hens at our partner farms. You can also add an extra herb bundle for $4, featuring freshly cut culinary sprigs such as dill, parsley, and cilantro hand-tied by Priya Nair. These add-ons are tucked neatly inside your wooden crate on packing morning, arriving alongside your regular vegetables without requiring separate shipping or additional packaging.

Transparent Membership and Included Delivery

Every price listed includes full door-to-door delivery within our twelve designated city neighbourhoods. We charge a $0 crate deposit; you simply hand back your empty wooden crate when receiving your next delivery. There are no registration fees, cancellation charges, or binding seasonal commitments. If you travel or need to adjust your kitchen schedule, you can pause, skip, or modify your subscription any time before the weekly Sunday 20:00 cutoff. Our member desk is available Monday through Friday from 9:00 to 17:00 to assist with any account inquiries.

pages.title: Delivery
pages.content:
Delivery

Delivery

Hatake Greens delivers fresh harvest crates to twelve city neighbourhoods situated within forty kilometres of our packing barn. We harvest at dawn and deliver directly to your doorstep the same afternoon.

Our Twelve Delivery Neighbourhoods

Our delivery vans operate within a strict 40-kilometre radius from our packing barn at 14 Orchard Lane in Wren Valley. We currently provide scheduled delivery service to twelve city neighbourhoods: Riverside, Old Mill, Canal Quarter, Northgate, Linden Park, Harbour Row, Elm Hill, Station Square, Westbrook, Fairfield, Southbank, and Kestrel Heights. By concentrating our delivery footprint in these specific districts, we maintain short travel times, conserve vehicle fuel, and ensure that produce harvested at sunrise arrives in pristine condition on city counters before evening.

Delivery Days and Afternoon Schedules

Deliveries take place twice weekly on Tuesday and Thursday between 14:00 and 19:00. Delivery lead Lena Sorensen oversees our drivers to ensure every crate is handled with respect and dropped off on schedule. If you are away from home during the delivery window, our drivers will place your wooden crate in a shaded, secure spot such as a covered porch, apartment vestibule, or with a neighbour. Because crates are packed only that morning, vegetables stay cool and crisp inside their protective unbleached wrapping until you unpack them.

Cutoff Deadlines and Crate Returns

Members enjoy complete flexibility over their delivery calendar. You can pause, skip an upcoming delivery, or switch between Tuesday and Thursday schedules through your online account. All adjustments, address changes, and pauses must be submitted before Sunday at 20:00 so our barn team can calculate exact harvest quantities with our six partner farms. When your next crate arrives, simply leave your previous empty wooden crate at your doorstep. We charge a $0 deposit and collect empty crates on each delivery run.

pages.title: Member Stories
pages.content:
Member Stories

Member Stories

Our members cook across different routines, from bustling family weeknights to quiet solo suppers. Here is how three households integrate our weekly harvest crates into their home kitchens.

The Park–Silva Household in Canal Quarter

Living in an apartment in Canal Quarter, the Park–Silva household consists of two working adults who joined Hatake Greens in 2021. Subscribing to the Standard crate at $32 / week, they receive nine varieties of greens, roots, and herbs every Tuesday afternoon. Having fresh vegetables delivered reliably has eliminated their midweek supermarket trips and inspired spontaneous weeknight cooking. They wash their salad greens immediately, store root vegetables in their pantry, and report that the produce stays crisp and fresh all the way through Sunday evening without wilting or going to waste.

Amara Diallo in Station Square

Amara Diallo lives alone in Station Square and subscribes to our Every-other-week standard crate for $34 / delivery. Before joining Hatake Greens, Amara frequently found supermarket produce spoiled before she could finish it. The disciplined portioning of nine fresh varieties allows her to roast roots during the first week and prepare crisp salads and herb-infused dishes during the second. She appreciates the simple Sunday 20:00 pause option when traveling for work, as well as the reliable afternoon delivery window managed by Lena Sorensen's team.

The Weiss Family in Linden Park

With two adults and three children, the Weiss family in Linden Park relies on the Large crate at $44 / week. Delivering twelve varieties of farm-fresh produce every Thursday between 14:00 and 19:00, the generous crate easily supplies their lively family dinners and school lunches. The children enjoy unpacking newly harvested carrots from Rafael Ortiz and fresh potatoes from Kwame Mensah, turning meal preparation into a shared family routine. The zero-deposit wooden crate exchange makes returning packaging effortless for a busy household.

pages.title: Questions & Answers
pages.content:
Questions & Answers

Questions & Answers

Find straightforward details below about our harvest schedule, crate options, delivery boundaries, and membership policies. If you have questions not covered here, our member desk is ready to help Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 17:00.

When are the vegetables harvested and delivered?

Our partner farms harvest all produce on Tuesday and Thursday mornings starting at 5:00 while the air is cool. Crate sorting and packing at our Wren Valley barn finish by 9:00, and crates are delivered to doorsteps the same afternoon between 14:00 and 19:00. This four-hour morning turnaround ensures vegetables arrive on your counter mere hours after harvest, without spending days in regional transit or supermarket cooling warehouses.

Which city neighbourhoods do you deliver to?

We deliver to twelve designated city neighbourhoods located within forty kilometres of our packing barn: Riverside, Old Mill, Canal Quarter, Northgate, Linden Park, Harbour Row, Elm Hill, Station Square, Westbrook, Fairfield, Southbank, and Kestrel Heights. By keeping our route network strictly within this 40-kilometre boundary, delivery lead Lena Sorensen and our drivers ensure prompt afternoon delivery without compromising the freshness of morning-picked greens.

What crate sizes are available and what do they cost?

We offer three crate sizes and a fortnightly schedule. The Small crate serves 1–2 people with 6 kinds of produce for $24 / week. The Standard crate suits 2–4 people with 9 kinds weighing about 4.5 kilograms for $32 / week. The Large crate feeds 4–6 people with 12 kinds for $44 / week. You may also select the Every-other-week standard crate for $34 / delivery.

How does the wooden crate exchange work?

We pack all produce into reusable wooden crates with a $0 crate deposit. When your weekly delivery arrives, simply place your empty wooden crate and folded paper wrap outside your door. Our delivery drivers collect the previous crate when dropping off your fresh box, returning it to our Wren Valley barn to be cleaned and repacked. This closed-loop system eliminates single-use cardboard and plastic packaging.

How do I pause, skip, or change my delivery?

You can pause your membership, skip a delivery, or switch between Tuesday and Thursday schedules at any time through your online member dashboard. Because our partner growers harvest to exact demand, all changes, skips, and pauses must be completed before Sunday at 20:00. Any adjustment made prior to Sunday evening takes effect for the coming week's harvest without penalty or extra fee.

Where do you source your vegetables?

All vegetables are grown by six independent partner farms situated within sixty kilometres of our packing barn at 14 Orchard Lane in Wren Valley. Co-founder Ines Calder coordinates directly with growers like Hana Moreau of Moreau Field, Rafael Ortiz of Ortiz Roots, Priya Nair of Nair Herb Garden, and Kwame Mensah of Mensah Hill. We never purchase produce from wholesale auctions or industrial distributors.

What add-ons can I order with my crate?

Members can add fresh farm staples to their regular vegetable delivery. We offer a dozen free-range eggs for $7, gathered from pasture hens at our partner farms, and an extra herb bundle for $4, hand-tied fresh on packing morning by Priya Nair. These add-ons are placed directly inside your wooden crate alongside your seasonal vegetables, arriving at your doorstep without separate packaging or additional delivery surcharges.

What if I live outside your current delivery area?

If your home is located outside our twelve delivery neighbourhoods, we invite you to register your address on our waitlist page. We review incoming location requests continually as we evaluate future route expansions from our packing barn in Wren Valley. When sufficient interest gathers in an adjacent district within 40 kilometres, waitlist members receive advance notification and early access to open delivery spots.

How much produce is included in a standard crate?

A standard crate contains nine distinct kinds of vegetables and greens, weighing approximately 4.5 kilograms in total. This quantity is intentionally balanced to supply a household of two to four people with a full week of daily home cooking. The selection includes crisp salad greens, hearty cooking leaves, root crops, alliums, and culinary herbs harvested fresh that morning from our six regional farm partners.

What happens if I am not home during delivery?

You do not need to be home to receive your box. Our drivers deliver between 14:00 and 19:00 on Tuesday and Thursday, placing your wooden crate in a sheltered location you specify, such as a covered front porch, building entryway, or with a neighbour. Unbleached paper wraps protect your greens from drafts and keep them cool until you unpack them into your kitchen.

When is your member desk available?

Our member desk is open Monday through Friday from 9:00 to 17:00 to answer questions, adjust account details, or assist with delivery instructions. You can reach out whenever you need help managing your subscription or coordinating crate returns. Outside these operating hours, you can update your delivery preferences or pause your membership directly through your account before the Sunday 20:00 cutoff.

Can I customize the specific vegetables in my crate?

Our crates are curated by our team based on what is ripe and harvested at 5:00 that morning across our six partner farms. By keeping the crate contents unified rather than customized, Tomas Achebe and our barn crew can pack crates by 9:00, while growers avoid surplus field waste. This disciplined approach maintains peak harvest freshness, fair pricing, and consistent seasonal flavour every week.

pages.title: Waitlist
pages.content:
Waitlist

Waitlist

If you live outside our current twelve delivery neighbourhoods, sign up here for early-access updates. We expand delivery routes thoughtfully to maintain our strict morning-harvest schedule.

Growing Beyond Our Current Twelve Neighbourhoods

Hatake Greens currently delivers to twelve city neighbourhoods within forty kilometres of our packing barn at 14 Orchard Lane in Wren Valley. Because our harvest happens at 5:00 and crates are delivered between 14:00 and 19:00 on the same day, we only expand into new districts when route logistics allow us to maintain this exact four-hour packing and delivery standard. Registering your location on our waitlist helps us map customer interest across surrounding districts and determine where new delivery routes can be opened sustainably.

Early Access for Emerging Routes

When a cluster of households registers in an adjacent neighbourhood within our forty-kilometre barn radius, delivery lead Lena Sorensen designs a viable van route. Waitlist members in that area receive priority invitations to choose a Tuesday or Thursday delivery slot before general registration opens. There is no cost or obligation to join the waitlist, and your contact information is used solely to notify you when vegetable crate delivery becomes available at your address.

Registering Your Home Address

To add your household to our expansion list, simply submit your name, street address, postal area, and preferred crate size. Our member desk reviews location entries weekly to monitor demand across regional borders. If you have questions regarding our delivery boundaries or membership options, our team is available Monday through Friday from 9:00 to 17:00 to assist you while you await route confirmation.

Email the member desk

pages.title: About Us
pages.content:
About Us

About Us

Founded in 2019, Hatake Greens connects local farmland directly with city kitchen counters through a disciplined same-day harvest routine. We operate from our central packing barn in Wren Valley, keeping the agricultural supply chain intentionally short.

Founded in 2019 at 14 Orchard Lane

Hatake Greens was founded in 2019 by Ines Calder and Tomas Achebe to create a direct link between regional farms and urban kitchens. Operating from our packing barn at 14 Orchard Lane in Wren Valley, we set out to eliminate the long storage times, wholesale warehouses, and excessive packaging typical of modern food supply chains. By establishing reliable weekly memberships, we provide local growers with steady demand while giving city households vegetables picked at peak morning vitality.

Why a Short Crate is a Full Week

We believe that a short crate is a full week. Instead of overwhelming households with dozens of random items that spoil in the crisper drawer, our standard crate provides nine carefully balanced kinds of vegetables and greens, weighing approximately 4.5 kilograms. Sourced exclusively from six partner farms within sixty kilometres, this curated selection gives two to four people exactly what they need for dependable home cooking, entirely free of food waste and unneeded excess.

The Team and Barn Operations

Our daily operations depend on a close-knit, dedicated team. Co-founder Ines Calder leads grower relations, collaborating closely with farmers like Hana Moreau, Rafael Ortiz, Priya Nair, and Kwame Mensah. Co-founder Tomas Achebe oversees barn operations at 14 Orchard Lane, guiding the washing and packing crew from 5:00 to 9:00 on harvest mornings. Delivery lead Lena Sorensen directs afternoon van routes across our twelve city neighbourhoods, while our member desk supports subscribers Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 17:00.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy

Privacy

How Hatake Greens handles the details you give us.

What we collect

We collect your name, delivery address, email, phone number and crate choice so that we can pack and deliver your crate. Waitlist entries contain the same contact details and your postal area.

How we use it

Your details are used only to run your membership: planning routes, delivering on Tuesday and Thursday between 14:00 and 19:00, and contacting you about your crate. We do not sell your information.

Your choices

You can ask the member desk, Monday to Friday 9:00–17:00, to see, correct or delete your details. Skips, swaps and pauses can be made until Sunday at 20:00.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
Terms

Terms

The plain terms of a Hatake Greens weekly membership.

Membership

A membership is a weekly or every-other-week crate: Small $24 per week, Standard $32 per week, Large $44 per week, or the every-other-week Standard at $34 per delivery. Delivery within our twelve neighbourhoods is included.

Changes and pauses

You may skip, swap or pause until Sunday at 20:00 before the next delivery. Crates are wooden and reusable, with a $0 deposit; please leave the empty crate at your door on the next delivery day.

Produce

Contents follow the harvest, so varieties vary by week. If something arrives damaged, tell the member desk and we will make it right on your next crate.
